entities.name: Acute viral bronchiolitis
observations: First-episode lower-airway illness after an upper-respiratory prodrome, with expiratory wheezing, tachypnea, retractions, and hypoxemia, is most consistent with acute viral bronchiolitis.
Routine bronchodilators, corticosteroids, racemic epinephrine, antibiotics, and hypertonic saline are not recommended for typical bronchiolitis without another indication.

entities.name: Bronchiolitis supportive care
observations: For persistent oxygen saturation around 90% with retractions, provide supplemental oxygen, gentle nasal saline/suctioning, and hydration support; use IV or nasogastric fluids when oral intake is unsafe or inadequate.
High-flow nasal cannula is an escalation option if hypoxemia or work of breathing persists despite standard oxygen, not the default initial treatment.

entities.name: Croup
observations: Croup is less likely because it typically causes barking cough and inspiratory stridor from upper-airway obstruction rather than predominantly expiratory wheezing.

entities.name: Bacterial pneumonia
observations: Bacterial pneumonia is less likely without focal lung findings, toxic appearance, or high/persistent fever, although hypoxemia warrants evaluation for severe disease and alternative diagnoses.
